author: blu
body: The on-disk layout of the fact log, in one place: the sizes, the field offsets, and the pure functions that read a field out of a sector buffer. DiskFacts (codex.os) writes and reads this layout; the compiler reads it through foreword FactDisk; before this chapter each carried its own copy of the offsets -- 32 for the kind, 66 for the timestamp, 74 for the content length -- and a change to one that the other did not follow was a divergence nothing caught until a work read back as garbage. The layout now has a single definition, and every reader and the writer ask it where a field is. The writer asking is the newer half: pack-fact-entry used to chain each field off the previous one's return value and step over the gap with a bare + 32, so the offsets these constants name were reachable only by adding the widths up. A writer that computes what a reader looks up is the same divergence with one side hidden.

author: blu
body: Only the PURE half lives here: constants and buffer decoders. Reading a sector off the disk is a Device.Block effect, and foreword is effect checked where DiskFacts (kernel) is exempt, so the sector walk that feeds these decoders stays with each reader. What is shared is the thing that drifts -- the shape -- not the loop that reads it.
